# Podranea brycei (N.E.Br.) Sprague

First published in D.Oliver & auct. suc. (eds.), Fl. Trop. Afr. 4(2): 515 (1906)

This species is accepted

The native range of this species is S. Tropical Africa. It is a shrub and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

### According to Flora Zambesiaca

Bignoniaceae, M. A. Diniz. Flora Zambesiaca 8:3. 1988

Morphology General Habit
    Scandent shrubs up to 10 m. high or subshrubs.
Morphology Branches
    Branches 4-angled, grooved minutely lepidote, pubescent only at the nodes.
Morphology Leaves
    Leaves imparipinnate, 13–27 cm. long, 4–7-jugate; petiole 2–6 cm. long; leaflet lamina 3.5–9 x 1.3–2.6 cm., narrowly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, longly acuminate at the apex, rounded to somewhat asymmetric at the base, grass green, inferior surface slightly lighter and glandular, margins entire or sometimes serrate-crenate uni- or bilaterally along the distal half; petiolules up to 1.5 cm. long in proximal pairs, decreasing progressively upwards.
    Stamens didynamous, included, with the staminode between the shorter pair; filaments adnate up to 1 cm. from the base of the corolla tube, densely pilose at the insertion points; anther-thecae divergent when mature, the connective apiculated and dorsaly crested.
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Disc
    Disk c. 1 mm. long, annular-cupular.
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Gynoecium Ovary
    Ovary c. 6 mm. long.
Morphology Reproductive morphology Fruits
    Capsule 35–48 x 1.5 cm., apex apiculate.
Morphology Reproductive morphology Seeds
    Seeds 0.6–1 x 3 cm. including the wings.
[FZ]
